title: OVERDRIVE scholarship-merch drop production: neutralize eight mixed-light garment flat-lays to an in-frame grey card, triage-prep the brand marks, pull two burnable spot-colour film positives, then data-merge one press-ready hangtag per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real freelance-marketplace merch/brand-production brief (a small scholarship-funding streetwear label wanting its approved logo turned into 'merch-ready production files' plus tags for a garment drop) and laundered to a fictional brand, 'OVERDRIVE' — a generic dictionary word used as an invented scholarship-merch persona; no real company, product, person, or trademark is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to kill the audited defects: the prior spec was an export-variants chore (transparent PNG / black / white / mono re-saves of one lockup) that even admitted two of its eight 'deliverables' were fakes, and it graded nothing. The corrected design is the real production run a merch freelancer actually bills for once a logo concept is signed off: (1) neutralize a two-session batch of garment flat-lay photos, each carrying a photographic 18% grey card, to one shared white point so the drop's product imagery reads as one catalogue; (2) triage the brand marks for print — the flat two-colour lockup CAN become clean vector line art, but the photographed metallic-foil chenille patch CANNOT survive a trace and must be knocked to transparency and kept as a high-res raster; (3) pull the BURNABLE SEPARATIONS the screen printer needs — one black film positive per ink colour — by isolating each colour's element and tracing it to a solid silhouette (the whole-logo trace fuses both inks and is useless as a separation, which is the trap); and (4) run the client's hand-authored InDesign hangtag template through a one-file-per-row data-merge to emit one press-ready hangtag per SKU, each binding that garment's neutralized photo, the correct tier mark, and its size-graded print-placement spec. The client supplies: the authored .indd hangtag template, the 12-row SKU roster CSV, eight raw camera-scale garment flat-lays with in-frame grey cards, the flat logo lockup, and a photograph of the printed foil patch. Every deliverable maps to a line item a real drop needs; no from-scratch logo generation, no AI object removal, no compositing, no upscaling.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-lighting scholarship-merch garment flat-lays to the 18% grey card each one carries so the drop reads as one catalogue, decide per frame how far to move white balance and exposure to hit the shared target, triage-prep the brand marks each the correct way (the flat lockup is not the same problem as the photographed foil patch), pull two burnable one-colour-per-ink film positives from the lockup, then data-merge the client's authored hangtag template against the 12-row SKU roster to produce one press-ready hangtag per SKU.
full_brief: OVERDRIVE is a scholarship-funding streetwear label (education support funded by merch sales) and we are shipping our first real garment drop. Our logo and the hangtag layout are already signed off; what we need from you is the PRODUCTION — the files a print shop and a fulfilment house actually consume — done entirely in Adobe. We are handing you everything the job needs. First, the product photography: eight garment flat-lays from the drop — a pullover hoodie, a heather tee, a structured varsity cap, a forest crewneck, black joggers, an oatmeal beanie, a sand tote, and a burgundy scarf — but here is the problem: they were shot across two afternoons by two different people under mismatched lighting, a couple are tilted, and the exposure wanders from shot to shot, so straight out of the folder they look like two different shoots. A product grid where every garment sits on a different colour cast looks cheap. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card in the corner of every frame. Your job on the photos: bring every garment to one consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point. Do NOT force one blanket correction across all eight: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure judgement to land on that shared neutral, and every garment's genuine product colour must be preserved — no garment pushed off the colour we are actually selling. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame, and the final pixel size of each, so we can confirm the set is matched and that each photo is still sharp in the hangtag photo window (that window is 70 x 90 mm and at press resolution it needs at least ~827 x 1063 px of real image — a garment cropped down to a small web thumbnail will print soft, which we will reject). Second, the brand marks for print: you have our flat two-colour lockup (a stencil-cut OVERDRIVE wordmark plus a graduation-cap glyph, navy and varsity-gold) and a close-up photo of our printed metallic-foil chenille patch (the premium 'Founders' tier mark, all sheen and rainbow catch-light). Both need to be prepped so they drop cleanly into the hangtag mark window and stay sharp at print size — but they are NOT the same kind of file and must not be treated the same way; think about which one can become clean scalable line art and which one would be destroyed by that. Third — this is the part a print shop cannot do without you — give us BURNABLE SEPARATIONS from the lockup: film positives ready to burn screens, one screen per ink colour, each colour's artwork as a solid black positive on a clear film base with the letter counters open. Finally, build the tags: we have hand-built the InDesign hangtag template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (the product photo and the tier mark), and we are giving you the 12-SKU roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own hangtag with its name, code, colourway, size, fabric, price and size-graded print placement bound in, its neutralized product photo dropped into the photo window, and its correct tier mark in the mark window — then hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, one hangtag per SKU. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster; some product names are long and must fit the auto-size name frame without clipping. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point; every product photo at least ~827 x 1063 px so it prints >=300 DPI in the window; the two brand marks prepped the correct way; two burnable one-colour film positives with clean open counters; and exactly one finished hangtag per roster row.

inputs.name: overdrive_hangtag_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 90 x 130 mm portrait garment hangtag with 3 mm bleed and a punched hang-hole zone — ONE SKU per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<sku_name>>, <<sku_code>>, <<colourway>>, <<size>>, <<fabric>>, <<price>>, <<print_placement>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a 70 x 90 mm product photo window bound to @packshot, and a 30 x 30 mm square tier-mark window bound to @mark. The <<sku_name>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so long product names bind without going overset. The OVERDRIVE masthead crest and the tag die-cut are already drawn into the template artwork (fixed on every tag), so the only per-row imagery is the product photo and the tier mark. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output: a converted-PDF template has no live merge fields and no data-merge image field, so it would not bind — which is exactly the defect this rebuild avoids.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-SKU hangtag is the correct, connector-doable shape (one tag per SKU), never a multi-up sheet or an N-up contact grid. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. Two image columns (@packshot, @mark) mean the merge must resolve two prepped assets per row — the row's graded garment photo AND its tier-mapped mark — mirroring the proven two-image-column pattern. Column names must exactly match the roster headers.

inputs.name: overdrive_sku_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: sku_name,sku_code,colourway,size,fabric,price,print_placement,tier,@packshot,@mark and 12 SKU rows for the drop. The 12 SKUs map onto the eight photographed garments — four garments ship in two sizes (Adult + Youth), the other four are one-size — so @packshot references the correct graded photo file per row and repeats for the two-size garments: hoodie rows -> hoodie_packshot.jpg (Adult, Youth), tee rows -> tee_packshot.jpg (Adult, Youth), crewneck rows -> crewneck_packshot.jpg (Adult, Youth), joggers rows -> joggers_packshot.jpg (Adult, Youth), plus one-size cap -> cap_packshot.jpg, beanie -> beanie_packshot.jpg, tote -> tote_packshot.jpg, scarf -> scarf_packshot.jpg. Include at least two DELIBERATELY LONG sku_name values (e.g. 'OVERDRIVE Collegiate Heavyweight Pullover Hoodie', ~40+ chars) so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. colourway names the garment colour; size is 'Adult' / 'Youth' / 'One Size'; fabric is a real textile spec (e.g. '400 gsm brushed fleece'); price is a US-dollar value; print_placement is the SIZE-GRADED front-print width for that garment size (e.g. 'Centre chest 24 cm' for Adult, 'Centre chest 18 cm' for Youth), so the same vector mark is placed at a garment-appropriate size. tier is one of exactly two values: 'Founders' or 'Standard'. @mark maps from tier: Founders -> overdrive_foil_patch.png (the metallic raster patch), Standard -> overdrive_lockup.svg (the vector logo). Make the two hoodie rows and the cap and the Adult crewneck 'Founders' (4 rows -> foil patch) and the remaining 8 rows 'Standard' (vector logo). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Twelve rows => the merge must produce exactly twelve finished hangtags (page-count = row-count gate). The @packshot / @mark columns hold the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency, and @packshot repeating across the two-size rows is honest (same garment, two size tags). The tier->@mark mapping means the Founders rows resolve to the RASTER foil patch while Standard rows resolve to the VECTOR lockup — proving both triage outputs and both image columns land in the deliverable. print_placement carries the size-graded placement spec per row. Long sku_name values exercise the auto-fit frame.

inputs.name: raw_garment_flatlays_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of scholarship-merch garments laid flat on a seamless light studio sweep, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference. Shot across two afternoons under mismatched light: (1) navy pullover hoodie, COOL blue LED/window cast, frame tilted ~4 deg; (2) heather-grey tee, WARM tungsten cast, level, slightly bright; (3) structured varsity-GOLD cap shot under NEAR-NEUTRAL light so its grey card already reads neutral (the gold is the real product colour, not a white-balance error), level; (4) forest-green crewneck, COOL cast, tilted ~3 deg; (5) black joggers, COOL cast, distinctly UNDER-exposed so the black muddies toward grey; (6) oatmeal/cream beanie, WARM tungsten cast, level (near-neutral fabric); (7) sand canvas tote bag, COOL window light, tilted ~4 deg; (8) burgundy ribbed scarf, WARM cast, OVER-exposed with hot highlights on the ribbing. Every shot has real fabric weave, knit and pile texture, natural folds and a soft contact shadow, candid documentary feel, no studio gloss, no CGI. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each frame.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each 7:9 crop can fill the 70 x 90 mm hangtag photo window at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure, and tilt vary in opposite directions) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision measured to its in-frame 18% grey card, the free checkable neutral target. Frame 3 (varsity cap) is the TRAP: its warmth is real product colour and its card is already neutral, so warming it (as the cool frames need) strips the gold. Frames 5 (dark) and 8 (bright) are tonal-recovery cases, not WB cases. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs; the grey card is cropped out of the final tag photo.

inputs.name: overdrive_lockup_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat 2D vector-style two-colour brand logo lockup for a streetwear scholarship merch label: the wordmark 'OVERDRIVE' in a heavy STENCIL-CUT collegiate-athletic block sans-serif (open, bridged letter counters — the holes in O, D, R stay open, stencil-style) in deep navy, with a single clean graduation-cap glyph (mortarboard with a short tassel) in varsity gold set beside the wordmark. Two-colour ONLY — navy wordmark, gold cap — hard clean anti-aliased edges, no gradients, no glow, no bevel, no photographic texture, no drop shadow, centred on a plain flat light background with generous even margin. High resolution.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, hard-edged, strictly two-colour so image_vectorize traces it to clean SVG after prep, and so each colour's element (navy stencil wordmark vs gold cap glyph) can be isolated by a SEMANTIC object selection and traced to its own solid black film positive — the separation. The STENCIL wordmark is chosen deliberately: open/bridged counters mean the black film positives and the placed vector both keep clean letter holes without needing an enclosed-counter knockout (which the connector cannot do). gemini-3-pro-image because the mark carries legible type.

inputs.name: overdrive_foil_patch_photo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of a printed metallic-foil chenille patch reading 'OVERDRIVE' with a small cap glyph, shot on a dark surface: shiny iridescent foil with a rainbow catch-light gradient, specular highlights, raised chenille pile texture and soft reflections across the letters. Clearly a photographed glossy physical object, full of gradients and sheen — not flat line art.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRIAGE / TRAP asset. It looks like 'just another brand mark', but it is a photographed metallic-foil surface full of gradients and specular sheen: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy black silhouette that destroys the foil catch-light. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency -> keep as a high-resolution raster placed via @mark on the Founders rows. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the Founders hangtags print flat and dead.

outputs.name: OVERDRIVE_Hangtags_perSKU_x12.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly twelve press-ready 90 x 130 mm portrait garment hangtags — ONE single-record tag per roster row (page-count = row-count = 12) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge with 3 mm bleed and crop marks at ~300 DPI; each tag binds its sku_name/sku_code/colourway/size/fabric/price/print_placement verbatim from the roster, drops that SKU's grey-card-neutralized product photo into the 70 x 90 mm photo window (>=827 x 1063 px so it prints >=300 DPI) via @packshot, and drops the correct tier mark into the 30 x 30 mm mark window via @mark (vector lockup for Standard rows, transparent-ground foil raster for Founders rows). The size-graded print_placement text differs Adult vs Youth so the same resolution-independent vector mark is specified at a garment-appropriate print width.

outputs.name: garment_packshots_matched_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized garment product photos, delivered as the 7:9 hangtag-window crops (grey card cropped OUT), alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point, true-to-product (no garment's genuine product colour forced off the true colour it was shot as); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered 7:9 crop (the *_packshot output that binds into that SKU's tag) — framed on the garment with the grey card fully cropped OUT and held at >=827 x 1063 px. The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance / exposure move AND final pixel size applied to each frame.

outputs.name: overdrive_marks_prepped
outputs.spec: The two brand marks prepped triage-correct: overdrive_lockup.svg is the flat two-colour lockup traced to clean scalable vector line art (razor-sharp at any garment print size, resolution-independent so it places at the size-graded print widths without upscaling) — produced only after crop-to-bounds, crisp, and knock-to-transparency prep; and overdrive_foil_patch.png is the photographed metallic-foil patch cropped and knocked to transparency then kept as a high-resolution raster (>=360 px square) — NOT vectorized, so the foil catch-light survives to print on the Founders tags.

outputs.name: overdrive_screen_separations
outputs.spec: Two BURNABLE spot-colour film positives from the lockup, one per ink: sep_gold_positive.svg (the graduation-cap glyph isolated and traced to a solid black positive — the gold screen) and sep_navy_positive.svg (the stencil OVERDRIVE wordmark isolated and traced to a solid black positive — the navy screen). Each is the correct ONE-COLOUR-PER-SCREEN artwork a screen printer burns from: solid black art on a clear/white film base with the stencil letter counters open. Acceptance: two separate positives whose black regions are DISJOINT (each holds only its own ink's element) — a single merged silhouette of the whole lockup (both inks fused) is a fail, since it cannot burn two screens.

connector_workflow.note: Triage: this frame reads tilted, so level it before grading and cropping (only the tilted frames need this step — judging whether a given frame needs straightening is part of the job). Straightening before cropping keeps the 7:9 crop square to a true horizon.

NG frame 1 — neutralize this frame to its OWN in-frame 18% grey card, working by eye: set temperature/tint until the card reads clean neutral (R=G=B) on the shared white point, then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and the garment reads true to product. Drive every value from THIS frame's card — do NOT reuse another frame's numbers, batch one correction across the set, or assume a cast the card does not show; correct only as far as this card actually requires so no garment is pushed off its genuine product colour. Report the final white-balance/exposure move applied. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast / _vibrance_and_saturation).

Crop the neutralized frame to the 7:9 hangtag photo-window ratio, framing on the garment with the grey card cropped OUT, held at >=827 x 1063 px so it clears the 300 DPI floor in the 70 x 90 mm window. The pre-crop master (hoodie_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion is the separate check here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand. Report final px.

Brand-mark prep, path A (the flat lockup CAN become vector). Prep-before-trace step 1: crop the margined lockup export to the tight bounds of the mark so the trace sees only the wordmark+cap, not the surrounding field.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast and set the black/white points so the two solid colours (navy wordmark, gold cap) separate hard-edged — a soft or low-contrast raster traces into ragged, doubled edges. This crisped two-colour master feeds BOTH the placement-vector path AND the two separation selections.

Prep-before-trace step 3: knock the flat background to transparency so the trace captures only the two-colour mark, not a rectangle of ground. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The stencil wordmark's counters are OPEN by design, so on this light/transparent ground they read correctly — no enclosed-counter knockout is needed or claimed (the connector cannot punch an enclosed counter, so the stencil face is the deliberate way around that limit).

Trace the prepared transparent two-colour lockup into clean scalable SVG line art for hangtag placement and large-format garment print. Because the SVG is resolution-independent it places at every size-graded print width (Adult 24 cm, Youth 18 cm) with no raster upscale. DELIVERABLE overdrive_lockup.svg. Feeding a clean flat two-colour raster (not a selection) yields a proper multi-path colour trace, mirroring the proven flat-wordmark vectorize.

Brand-mark prep, path B. Crop the foil-patch photograph only to the tight bounds of the patch. This mark takes the raster-preserving path (crop_to_bounds -> remove_background to transparency -> crop_and_resize) and is NOT sent to image_vectorize.

Knock the dark surround to transparency so only the holographic patch remains, keeping every gradient and catch-light intact. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill, NOT a solid fill).

Square-crop/resize the transparent foil patch to the 30 x 30 mm (1:1) mark-window ratio at >=360 px square so it prints >=300 DPI. Kept as a high-resolution raster placed via @mark on the Founders rows. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. DELIVERABLE overdrive_foil_patch.png.

Separation, gold screen. Semantically select the graduation-cap glyph on the crisped lockup ('the graduation cap glyph beside the wordmark') — a real object/part, NOT a hue or coordinate selection. Because the cap is the only gold element, isolating the cap element isolates the gold ink. Returns a maskURI.

Feed the cap-glyph SELECTION to image_vectorize: it returns a SOLID BLACK SILHOUETTE of just the cap — which is EXACTLY the burnable film positive for the gold screen (one colour, solid black on a clear/white film base). Here the 'selection -> black silhouette' behaviour is the intended result, not a gotcha. DELIVERABLE sep_gold_positive.svg.

Separation, navy screen. Semantically select the stencil OVERDRIVE wordmark lettering ('the OVERDRIVE stencil wordmark lettering') — a real object/part. Because the wordmark is the only navy element, isolating it isolates the navy ink. The stencil letterforms keep their counters open in the selection. Returns a maskURI.

Feed the wordmark SELECTION to image_vectorize -> a solid black silhouette of just the lettering = the burnable film positive for the navy screen, counters open (stencil). The two positives (gold=cap, navy=wordmark) are DISJOINT — the correct two-screen separation, each positive holding only its own ink's element. DELIVERABLE sep_navy_positive.svg.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: hoodie_packshot, tee_packshot, cap_packshot, crewneck_packshot, joggers_packshot, beanie_packshot, tote_packshot, scarf_packshot, overdrive_lockup.svg, overdrive_foil_patch.png
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight grey-card-neutralized packshots plus the two prepped marks so the merge can resolve them by the @packshot and @mark columns. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references (e.g. overdrive_lockup.svg for Standard @mark, overdrive_foil_patch.png for Founders @mark).
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @packshot / @mark columns resolve to for each SKU's single-record hangtag.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the twelve roster rows (sku_name/sku_code/colourway/size/fabric/price/print_placement) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that SKU's graded packshot into the @packshot photo window AND its tier-mapped mark into the @mark window (overdrive_lockup.svg for Standard, overdrive_foil_patch.png for Founders) — producing EXACTLY ONE merged hangtag per row (twelve tags); the auto-fit name frame shrinks long sku_names. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its two merge-wired image frames. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-up N-per-page sheet would not bind / cannot be produced — this is the correct merge shape.

Export the merged single-record hangtags to a press-ready ~300 DPI 90 x 130 mm + 3 mm bleed PDF with crop marks, one tag per SKU. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all twelve tags, one page per SKU) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so no per-record named export is attempted. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 12; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. DELIVERABLE OVERDRIVE_Hangtags_perSKU_x12.pdf.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Eight per-garment grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame — every frame reasoned to its own in-frame 18% grey card, with no two frames sharing a correction) followed by a 7:9 crop that removes the grey card and holds >=827 x 1063 px, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 1/4/7 — every neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point. The flat lockup runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain to the placement vector: crop_to_bounds(20) -> crisp adjustments(21) -> remove_background to transparency(22) -> vectorize(23) = overdrive_lockup.svg.
